speaker: NARRATOR
text: [darker, lower, slow] Now. Think about who LOVES the idea that heart disease comes from your personality. From your stress.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [pointed, dry] And not from, say... smoking.

speaker: AD VOICE
text: [bright, polished, too smooth] Tense? Wound up? Long day at the office? [beat] Take a moment. Light up. Relax.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [investigative, steady] Decades later, researchers dug through millions of pages of tobacco industry documents. And they found something.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [quiet, deliberate] In 1958, Hans Selye, the father of stress, wrote to a tobacco company asking for money.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [flat] He got it. A lot of it. [quicker] Over the years the industry funded his work, and it used stress research in court to argue that something else was making people sick.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [pause] He didn't publicly declare those ties.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [wry, almost tired] And Type A? A later study found the tobacco industry had been a major funder of that research too.

speaker: YOU
text: [quiet, stunned] So the cigarette companies helped sell me my stress.

speaker: AD VOICE
text: [distant, fading, like a memory] Light up. Relax.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [gently] They helped sell you a story about it. That stress is something that happens TO you. Something that breaks you. And that you need something to take the edge off.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [slow, heavy] And that story might be doing more harm than the stress itself.
